subsystems.name: Beam source
subsystems.role: generates the coherent light or microwaves that carry the energy.

subsystems.name: Phased array and beam director
subsystems.role: combines many emitters into a single steerable beam and holds it on target.
parts: large aperture mirrors or antenna elements

subsystems.name: Sail or thrust plate
subsystems.role: receives the beam and converts it into thrust, either by photon pressure or by heating a propellant.
parts: heat exchanger and propellant injection (thermal mode)

subsystems.name: Vehicle
subsystems.role: carries the payload and maintains attitude so the sail stays facing the beam.
parts: attitude control thrusters or reaction wheels

subsystems.name: Tracking and control
subsystems.role: senses the sail's position and feeds corrections to the beam director.

buildSteps.title: Build the beam array
buildSteps.detail: Many laser or microwave emitters are mounted side by side and phase-locked so their beams add up coherently into one powerful beam.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the sail
buildSteps.detail: A reflective film just tens of nanometres thick is deposited on a lightweight frame, then tensioned and packaged for launch.

buildSteps.title: Integrate power and cooling
buildSteps.detail: The array needs massive electrical power and cooling; capacitors or flywheels store energy for short pulses if the source is pulsed.

buildSteps.title: Test in a vacuum chamber
buildSteps.detail: A small sail is suspended in vacuum and hit with a scaled-down beam to measure thrust, stability and beam-riding behaviour.

buildSteps.title: Demonstrate beam-riding
buildSteps.detail: For launch, a small craft is pushed by a ground beam through the lower atmosphere; for space sails, a beam from a ground station propels a satellite in low orbit.

buildSteps.title: Scale to operational use
buildSteps.detail: The array is enlarged and the sail made lighter until the system can launch payloads to orbit or accelerate a gram-scale probe to a fraction of light speed.

buildSteps.title: Operate and track
buildSteps.detail: During a mission, tracking radar or lidar keeps the beam centred on the sail, adjusting phase and pointing thousands of times per second.

prerequisites.tech: High-power, efficient lasers or microwave sources
prerequisites.why: lab and industrial lasers exist, but scaling to megawatts with high wall-plug efficiency remains a challenge.
thin films are made today, but they must survive launch and stay flat under beam pressure.

prerequisites.tech: Phased array beam combining and adaptive optics
prerequisites.why: used in astronomy and defence, but not yet at the power and precision needed for propulsion.
keeping a beam on a fast-moving sail requires radar/lidar and control loops far faster than current space-tracking systems.
microelectronics and miniaturised instruments already exist, though they must be hardened for high-radiation or interstellar environments.

pathway.milestone: laboratory demonstrations of laser sails and microwave thermal thrusters, plus pulsed-laser launch experiments
pathway.unlocks: proof that a beam can push a small object in a controlled way.

pathway.milestone: orbital demonstration of beamed propulsion for small satellites, such as orbit raising or deorbiting
pathway.unlocks: operation in space, where beam-riding and tracking can be tested without atmospheric interference.

pathway.milestone: ground-to-orbit launch of a small payload using a beamed thermal thruster
pathway.unlocks: a reusable, propellant-free first stage that could cut launch costs.

pathway.milestone: large ground array accelerating a gram-scale lightsail to a fraction of light speed, as envisioned by concepts such as Breakthrough Starshot
pathway.unlocks: interstellar probes able to reach nearby stars within a human lifetime.
